_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MOSTLY ROCK AND WATER -- there is NO foliage in this tile at all: zero trees, zero leaf masses, nothing for a foliage mask to grab. What it holds is the TRESTLE BRIDGE (棧道, a plank road on wooden piles) running across the upper third, the tail of the moving party crossing above it (a robed gentleman, a pack deer, a porter), a wall of cliff down the left, a long raking boulder bank on the right, and the RIVER filling the bottom half as bare silk with ripple lines curling round standing boulders. Four collector seals are stamped down the left margin. The only motion available here is water and robes. A colour-threshold masker will find the ochre wash on the right-hand bank and the dark 苔點 moss dots along every rock ridge and call them leaves -- that is exactly the defect that got rejected. There is nothing green in this tile.

objects.name: robed gentleman in a dark-bordered white robe, top centre
objects.note: the largest figure in the tile, clipped at the waist by the top edge -- only the skirt and hem are in frame, which is convenient: the hem is exactly the part that should move and the face is not here to deform

objects.name: figure in a plain white robe walking the upper path
objects.note: clipped at the waist by the top edge; legs, hem and one shoe visible on the pale path

objects.name: tan pack animal (deer) on the upper path
objects.note: an ANIMAL, not a person -- Ge Hong's deer, ochre body on four thin dark legs, clipped at the shoulder by the top edge. kind 'figure' because the enum has no animal. Motion 'none': a walk cycle is not on the table and anything less than one looks broken. Treat as a rigid cel

objects.name: pale grey robe of a further figure behind the gentleman
objects.note: UNCERTAIN -- a rounded grey shape overlapping the gentleman's right shoulder that reads as another person's sleeve or a carried bundle. Too clipped by the top edge to settle here; t004/t005 (the row below) will not help, but the full-scroll view will

objects.name: the plank bridge on wooden piles crossing the tile
objects.note: 棧道 -- a ruled timber structure: deck, cross-braced piles, and a deck edge fringed with heavy round moss dots. RIGID, every stroke of it. The dot fringe along the deck is the single most tree-like texture in the tile and is architecture, not leaves. The bridge continues into t001 at the left edge

objects.name: porter walking right with a rolled bundle on his back
objects.note: SAME MAN as 'porter-with-bundle-left' in t001 -- the tiles overlap by 264 master px and he is in both. Do not animate him twice out of phase

objects.name: the cliff wall filling the left of the tile
objects.note: 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes running with the stone's fall, capped with dark moss dots along every ridge. NEVER animate. The moss dots are the trap: they are round, repeated, clustered and dark, exactly like leaf glyphs, but they sit ON the rock contour with no branch under them and carry no green or ochre wash

objects.name: rock shelf and boulders below the bridge piles
objects.note: the stack the water pours through; the piles land on it

objects.name: band of heavy dark dashes on the rock lip under the bridge
objects.note: GENUINELY UNCERTAIN and the reason this object exists. Two rows of fat elongated dots strung along the lip of the rock shelf. Read at 3x they are 大混點 accent dots following the stone's contour -- no trunk, no branch, no stem, no wash of any colour -- so I have called them rock furniture (moss/scrub on stone) and NOT foliage. The competing reading is a line of very distant scrub. Either way: do not put this box in the foliage mask. If a later pass wants distant scrub motion it should re-examine this at full resolution first

objects.name: the pale chute of water dropping through the rocks under the bridge
objects.note: 留白 -- bare silk between two dark rock lips, painted by omission. Feeds the river below. Low-contrast, so a motion pass here must move the EDGES of the rock lips' reflections, not a texture that isn't there

objects.name: the long raking boulder bank down the right side
objects.note: stacked rounded boulders in raking parallel hemp-fibre strokes, carrying a faint OCHRE wash. The ochre is the second trap in this tile: it is the same yellow that autumn leaves carry elsewhere in the scroll, and here it is stone. NEVER animate

objects.name: the river filling the bottom half of the tile
objects.note: bare silk with fine ripple lines that ring each standing boulder. The lines ARE the water -- move them as one surface, never as cards, and keep the rings anchored to their rocks

objects.name: the large boulder standing mid-river
objects.note: ringed by its own ripple lines -- the rock holds still and the rings move around it

objects.name: the small paired rocks in the water, upper left of the river
objects.note: two low humps with a single ripple ring

objects.name: boulder at the left edge of the river
objects.note: clipped by the left edge

objects.name: the flat table-like slab in the lower river
objects.note: the nearest rock in the tile and the clearest read of the water plane -- ripples pass in front of and behind it

objects.name: boulders in the water at the bottom right corner
objects.note: clipped by the bottom and right edges; continues into t004/t005

objects.name: tall rectangular collector seal, upper left margin
objects.note: vermilion seal stamped on the silk. Seals are FLAT ON THE PICTURE PLANE -- they belong to the surface, not the landscape, so they must not take parallax or they will swim across the rock

objects.name: square collector seal, middle left margin
objects.note: sits on bare water silk; same plane rule as the other seals

objects.name: square collector seal below the middle one
objects.note: same plane rule

objects.name: large multi-character seal at the bottom left corner
objects.note: the biggest seal in the tile, clipped by the bottom edge and continuing into t004. Same plane rule
